classification.difficultyReason: Choose a taught 60-degree or right-angle construction, bisect as needed, and recognise that 150 and 135 degrees can be obtained by taking supplements of constructed angles.

content.prompt: Use only compasses, a straight edge and a sharpened pencil. Each part below requires a combination of constructions. Draw an interval $AB$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Construct angles of $30^\circ$ and $15^\circ$ at point $A$.

answer.short: $30^\circ$ and $15^\circ$ at $A$, with construction arcs retained.
answer.worked:
Construct an equilateral triangle $ABC$ on $AB$: draw arcs of radius $AB$ centred at $A$ and $B$, and join their intersection $C$ to $A$. Then $\angle CAB=60^\circ$.

Bisect $\angle CAB$ using equal-radius arcs from the points where an arc centred at $A$ meets its arms. Join $A$ to the intersection of those arcs to obtain a $30^\circ$ ray. Repeat the angle-bisection construction between that ray and $AB$ to obtain a $15^\circ$ ray.

$$\begin{align*}\tfrac12\times60^\circ&=30^\circ\\\tfrac12\times30^\circ&=15^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Authored sample construction showing the equilateral-triangle ray and its successive bisectors; dashed compass arcs remain visible.
spec.mathematics: The rays at A make 60, 30 and 15 degrees with AB.

answer.short: $45^\circ$ and $22\frac12^\circ$ at $A$, with construction arcs retained.
answer.worked:
Extend $BA$ beyond $A$. Draw an arc centred at $A$ meeting the extended line at two points equidistant from $A$. From those points draw equal-radius arcs that intersect above the line. Join their intersection to $A$ to construct a right angle.

Use the angle-bisection construction to bisect the right angle, then bisect the angle between the new ray and $AB$.

$$\begin{align*}\tfrac12\times90^\circ&=45^\circ\\\tfrac12\times45^\circ&=22\tfrac12^\circ\end{align*}$$

answer.short:
$150^\circ$ at $A$.

Construct $30^\circ$ and take its supplement.
answer.worked:
Construct an equilateral triangle on $AB$ and bisect its angle at $A$ to obtain a $30^\circ$ ray. Extend this ray backwards through $A$. The angle between $AB$ and the backward ray is supplementary to $30^\circ$.

$$180^\circ-30^\circ=150^\circ$$

Retain the compass arcs used to construct and bisect the $60^\circ$ angle.

answer.short:
$135^\circ$ at $A$.

Construct $45^\circ$ and take its supplement.
answer.worked:
Extend $BA$ beyond $A$ and construct a perpendicular at $A$ by bisecting the straight angle. Bisect the resulting right angle to obtain a $45^\circ$ ray. Extend this ray backwards through $A$. The angle between $AB$ and the backward ray is supplementary to $45^\circ$.

$$180^\circ-45^\circ=135^\circ$$

Retain the compass arcs used for the perpendicular and the angle bisector.
